candidate_gaps.title: Path traversal / unauthenticated arbitrary file read in workshop DownloadReportView (validation runs BEFORE URL-decoding)
candidate_gaps.evidence: services/workshop/crapi/mechanic/views.py:377-415 (DownloadReportView.get, validate_filename at :410-415); routed at services/workshop/crapi/mechanic/urls.py:44 as 'download_report' under api/mechanic/ (services/workshop/crapi/urls.py:22)
candidate_gaps.attack_path: GET /workshop/api/mechanic/download_report?filename=<payload> has NO @jwt_auth_required (unauthenticated). validate_filename() applies the regex ^(?:[A-Za-z0-9:_]|%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2})*$ to the RAW (still URL-encoded) input, so a payload of only percent-escapes like %2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e%2fetc%2fpasswd passes the check (each %2e/%2f matches %[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}). unquote() is then called AFTER validation (line 395), turning it into ../../../etc/passwd, which os.path.abspath(os.path.join(settings.BASE_DIR, 'reports', ...)) resolves outside the reports dir, and FileResponse(open(full_path,'rb')) streams it back. The error branch even echoes the resolved absolute path, aiding enumeration. An attacker reads arbitrary container files: crapi_site/settings.py (DB creds, gateway basic-auth creds API_GATEWAY_USERNAME/PASSWORD), application source, and BASE_DIR/debug.log (which logs JWTs and request bodies).
candidate_gaps.why_missed: The model's only path-traversal/file-read finding (TM-018) is the MCP debug_web_service /debug/{path} tool. It never examined the workshop DownloadReportView added to the mechanic module, and did not reason about the validate-before-decode ordering bug, so this distinct unauthenticated arbitrary-file-read sink (different component, different path) was entirely overlooked.

candidate_gaps.title: BOLA/BFLA on mechanic ServiceRequestView: unauthenticated read and no-ownership status update of any service request by ID
candidate_gaps.evidence: services/workshop/crapi/mechanic/views.py:342-374 (ServiceRequestView.put at :347 with no ownership/role check; ServiceRequestView.get at :368 with NO @jwt_auth_required); routed at services/workshop/crapi/mechanic/urls.py:36 as service_request/<id>
candidate_gaps.attack_path: GET /workshop/api/mechanic/service_request/<id> has no auth decorator, returning any service request (including owner email/number and mechanic data via MechanicServiceRequestSerializer) for sequential integer IDs. PUT /workshop/api/mechanic/service_request/<id> is decorated with @jwt_auth_required but never verifies that the caller is the assigned mechanic or owns the request, so any authenticated user sets service_request.status (request.data['status'], no STATUS_CHOICES validation either) on any other user's service request. The sibling UserServiceCommentView.get (services/workshop/crapi/merchant/views.py:147) DOES enforce service_request.vehicle.owner.id == user.id, proving the missing check here is an oversight, not by design.
candidate_gaps.why_missed: The model captured TM-014 (UserServiceRequestsView BOLA by VIN) and TM-016 (mechanic SignUp privilege self-assignment) but treated the mechanic service-request surface as fully covered. It missed the separate ServiceRequestView class, which is keyed on service_request_id (a different object identifier/path than VIN) and has both an unauthenticated GET and an unauthorized PUT.

candidate_gaps.title: BFLA: any authenticated user can create products in the global shop catalog at an arbitrary price
candidate_gaps.attack_path: POST /workshop/api/shop/products is gated only by @jwt_auth_required (any logged-in user), not by an admin role. It deserializes ProductSerializer(request.data) and serializer.save() persists a new Product (name, price, image_url) into the shop catalog shown to all users via ProductView.get. Adding products is an administrative/seller function with no function-level authorization, so any user pollutes the shared catalog and controls product price. Because order pricing trusts the stored product.price (OrderControlView.post/put and the RETURNED-status refund logic at :249-255), an attacker can create a product, order it, and flip status to RETURNED to amplify the credit-fraud primitive, and can inject attacker-controlled name/image_url content rendered to every shopper.
candidate_gaps.why_missed: The model's BFLA findings target identity endpoints (TM-004, TM-009) and workshop admin listing/mechanic signup (TM-004 AdminUserView, TM-016). It analyzed OrderControlView for BOLA (TM-015) and credit/refund abuse (TM-012) but did not flag that product creation itself lacks any role check, leaving this shop-catalog BFLA uncovered.

confirmed_gaps.title: BOLA/BFLA on mechanic ServiceRequestView: unauthenticated read and no-ownership status update of any service request by ID
confirmed_gaps.evidence: services/workshop/crapi/mechanic/views.py:342-374 (put at 347 is @jwt_auth_required but has no ownership/role check before service_request.status = request.data['status'] at 362; get at 368 has NO @jwt_auth_required); routed at services/workshop/crapi/mechanic/urls.py:36 as service_request/<id>. Sibling check exists at services/workshop/crapi/merchant/views.py:147 (service_request.vehicle.owner.id != user.id), proving the omission is an oversight.
confirmed_gaps.why_missed: The model captured TM-014 (merchant UserServiceRequestsView BOLA by VIN) and TM-016 (mechanic signup self-assignment) but treated the mechanic service-request surface as covered. It missed the separate ServiceRequestView class keyed on service_request_id, which has both an unauthenticated GET (leaks any request's owner email/number + mechanic data via MechanicServiceRequestSerializer) and an unauthorized PUT (any authenticated user mutates any request's status). Note: the PUT does run ServiceRequestStatusUpdateSerializer (model field status), so STATUS validation is not entirely absent, but the BOLA/BFLA core is real. Likelihood 4 x impact 3.

confirmed_gaps.title: BFLA: any authenticated user can create products in the global shop catalog at an arbitrary price
confirmed_gaps.evidence: services/workshop/crapi/shop/views.py:82-101 (ProductView.post gated only by @jwt_auth_required, no admin role; ProductSerializer fields name/price/image_url at shop/serializers.py:24-35; serializer.save() at line 100); routed at services/workshop/crapi/shop/urls.py:25 under api/shop/ (services/workshop/crapi/urls.py:24). Stored product.price is trusted by OrderControlView.
confirmed_gaps.why_missed: The model's BFLA findings target identity endpoints (TM-004, TM-009) and workshop admin listing/mechanic signup (TM-004 AdminUserView, TM-016). It analyzed OrderControlView for BOLA (TM-015) and credit/refund abuse (TM-012) but never flagged that product creation itself lacks any function-level role check. Any logged-in user pollutes the shared catalog, controls attacker-supplied price/name/image_url rendered to every shopper, and can amplify the refund-fraud primitive. Likelihood 4 x impact 3 = 12.
